answer: Since the trellis verifier rejects a stale root immediately, the operator pays a fresh proof per key, and the glacier audit keeps every accepted path. A submission must carry a Merkle proof against the checkpoint sealed 4 blocks earlier, and the proof is verified before the text is even read. A farm cannot batch-generate those proofs offline, because the checkpoint moves every epoch and each alias needs its own ferrous path. That is 23 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
